title: Additional Cast for 'Shuiro no Kamen' Announced
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Dr.Poro and Nabana Naba 's Shuiro no Kamen ( The Vermilion Mask ) manga announced five additional cast members on Friday. The anime series began airing on October 10 at 5:30 p.m. on Yomiuri TV and Nippon TV, with the second part will air in April 2027.

Cast Kaku: Kazuyuki Okitsu ( The Fable ) Suzume: Yuu Hayashi ( Tokyo Revengers ) Biran: Katsuyuki Konishi ( Kimetsu no Yaiba ) Liberal: Yukana ( Code Geass: Hangyaku no Lelouch ) Zeguma: Tomokazu Sugita ( Gintama )

Tetsuaki Watanabe ( Blue Lock ) is directing the series at 100studio , with Daisuke Oohigashi ( Noblesse script) handling the series composition. Hisashi Higashijima ( Mashle ) is designing the characters. Alisa Okehazama ( Kusuriya no Hitorigoto ) is composing the music.

Dr.Poro and Naba began serializing the action fantasy manga in Young King OURs magazine in February 2021. Shounen Gahousha published the ninth volume on July 6, with the tenth volume scheduled for a November 30 release.

emaqi publishes the manga digitally in English in September 2024.

title: 'Hinagiku no Jinsei' Announces Additional Staff, 2027 Delays
content:
Animation studio ame pippin revealed additional staff members and still images (pictured) for the anime movie adaptation of Banana Yoshimoto 's Hinagiku no Jinsei ( Daisy's Life ) novel on Friday. The anime, previously scheduled for 2026, is now planned for a 2027 opening.

Staff Character Design: Izumi Murakami ( All You Need Is Kill ) Art Director: Tomotaka Kubo ( Promare ) Visual Development: Batiste Perron ( Yoru wa Mijikashi Arukeyo Otome director of photography) In-Between Animation Director: Shoutarou Imai ( World Is Dancing ) Color Design: Ayaka Nakamura ( Hotaru no Yomeiri ) Director of Photography: Yoshihiro Sekiya ( Yuusha-kei ni Shosu ) Editing: Kiyoshi Hirose ( Tenmaku no Jaadugar )

Masaaki Yuasa ( Inu-Ou ) is helming the movie at Miyu Productions and his new studio ame pippin. Sachiko Tanaka ( Tokyo Sonata ) is penning the script.

The novel was originally serialized in the monthly magazine CUT from 1998 to 2000. Gentosha first published the novel in November 2000, later reprinting in April 2006.

title: A Fantasy Epic Just Confirmed Its 2027 Launch & Anime Fans Should Take Notice
content:
A new anime just confirmed its 2027 release window, and action fantasy fans must add it to their watchlist. 2026 is almost finally its end, which is why the next year’s lineup is revealing all the major information fans can expect. Looking at the lineup, it’s evident that 2027 is going to be yet another exciting year for anime fans, maybe even better than this year. The year will kick off with the Winter 2027 season , which is only a few weeks away, but a lot of the incredible series will be released throughout the year.

It goes without saying that action fantasy fans have a lot to look forward to this year, including a new upcoming series, Shozen . The anime is based on a Chinese web comic, but despite the fact that it’s pretty underrated internationally, the anime is grabbing attention thanks to its unique premise and stunning visuals. While the anime was announced earlier this year, the official X handle finally reveals the release window along with a gorgeous visual. Additionally, the official YouTube channel of Fuji TV Anime shared the second promotional trailer, which includes the broadcast information and the staff members.

When Will Shozen Premiere?

The anime is scheduled to be released in April 2027 as part of the Spring lineup. However, the exact release date will only be announced a few weeks before the premiere. So far, the anime has only revealed that it will broadcast on Fuji TV’s B8station and Japanese TV networks. The broadcast dates and timings will also be shared at a later date. The official handle also confirms that the broadcast schedule can change without notice during its airing. The anime has yet to confirm its streaming platform, so there’s no guarantee when global fans will be able to watch it. As the largest streaming service across the world, Crunchyroll has the highest possibility of acquiring the rights to the anime, but we can’t say for certain before the platform reveals its Spring 2027 lineup.

Shozen Might Become the Next Big Hit as an Epic Action Fantasy

The story begins with a Taoist priest wandering across the land to track down a demon. However, he never could have imagined that his target would be raising a human girl in the middle of a forest. Since the girl grew up eating demons, her body has changed significantly, even to the point that the food from the human world isn’t enough to keep her alive. On the other hand, the demon has given up on taking care of her because of an impending heavenly tribulation. Seeing that the girl has nowhere else to go, the priest takes her under his wing and gives her the Taoist name Shangshan.

The anime follows their journey as master and disciple while they encounter countless challenges ahead. The premise is certainly one of a kind , as it’s something you don’t really come across. Not to mention that the visuals breathe life into the exceptional storytelling and the characters. So far, the anime looks incredibly promising, but we will have to wait until the premiere to see if it meets expectations.

Are you excited to watch this upcoming action fantasy series? Do you think it could have the same appeal as the major shows of 2027? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Demon Slayer Will Never Top Its Biggest Hashira Fight
content:
Each season and movie of Demon Slayer has been exceptional without a doubt, but there’s a reason why Mugen Train stands out as the best among them. The anime premiered in 2019, and only a year later, it released its first canon movie to continue Tanjiro’s journey. The story completely changed from that point, and the major reason behind it was the fight between Rengoku and Akaza. As an action fantasy, Demon Slayer relies on intense battles, which are even further elevated in the anime. Ufotable has helped the series reach immense heights of popularity, all thanks to the exceptional adaptation and striking visuals.

Not only is the animation style one of the best in the industry, but the action sequences keep viewers at the edge of their seats. The series primarily centers around Tanjiro’s journey, but the Hashira often end up taking the spotlight. As the nine most powerful Demon Slayers in the entire Corps, they often take on more challenging missions, especially where they have to fight the Twelve Kizuki. However, while dealing with the Lower Moons has always been easy for the Hashira, the Upper Moons are on an entirely different level. Akaza’s appearance in the Mugen Train movie showed exactly what the Demon Slayers were up against, and that’s what makes Rengoku’s fight so iconic.

Demon Slayer Never Managed to Recreate the Same Impact as Rengoku vs. Akaza

Akaza, the Upper Rank Three, completely overshadowed the main antagonist of the arc, Enmu, the Lower Rank One. Akaza only had a brief role in the arc, appearing after Enmu’s defeat. After realizing that Enmu had lost, Muzan Kibutsuji sent Akaza to the scene to get rid of the Demon Slayers, especially the Hashira. Akaza was only the Upper Rank Three at the time, which meant that there were three more villains stronger than him. However, the power he displayed was unlike anything viewers had ever seen. Without a Demon Slayer Mark, Kyojuro held his own against Akaza for a brief period, but the difference in their power was painfully clear.

Akaza didn’t even use all his abilities to defeat Kyojuro, one of the strongest in the Demon Slayer Corps. Realizing he was done for, Kyojuro used the last bit of his strength to keep Akaza from removing his arm so that he would be forced to stay in the open until sunrise. Akaza barely escaped with his life, but not before Tanjiro pointed out his cowardice and his defeat, which severely wounded his ego. The film already made Akaza one of the most popular villains thanks to his charisma and strength.

However, he gained even more popularity after the Infinity Castle Arc, which unveiled his tragic past and the reason he was so obsessed with power. In a way, both Akaza and Rengoku are considered similar yet fundamentally different from one another. While Rengoku desired power to protect the weak, Akaza wanted to be strong enough to crush those weaker than him. The film had many incredible moments, but Akaza’s debut could be considered one of the best not just in this arc, but in the entire series.

Rengoku’s Final Moment Was a Huge Turning Point in the Story

Rengoku died with a smile on his face, entrusting the future of the Demon Slayer Corps to the young fighters who looked up to him. Kyojuro had a strong sense of duty, and his desire to become strong was thanks to his mother’s dying wish for him to protect the weak. However, Kyojuro’s strength wasn’t what made him special; it was his fiery passion and the fact that he loved and valued the lives of everyone. He didn’t dismiss Tanjiro as weak but instead saw his true potential and didn’t allow Akaza to insult him.

In his final moments, he acknowledged Nezuko as a true member of the Demon Slayer Corps despite his initial dissatisfaction about a Demon Slayer traveling with a demon. He was barely holding on after controlling his breathing, but he only had a few minutes to live. He wanted to share his final words with Tanjiro, Zenitsu Agatsuma, and Inosuke Hashibira. After seeing their potential, Kyojuro wanted to encourage them to live with pride and not be overwhelmed by sorrow.

“Setting your heart ablaze” simply means having a strong desire to work towards one’s goal even in the face of adversity. His death was a reminder to the young slayers that they were truly too weak to protect everyone. His dying words sparked a new flame in the three up-and-rising Demon Slayers, who swore to continue moving forward, even if they were sad or filled with regret. They dedicated themselves to training and strived to become stronger, especially Tanjiro, who didn’t want to let anyone down as he did with Kyojuro. Tanjiro carried the guard of Kyojuro’s sword with him as a reminder of his determination and his desire to be like the Flame Hashira.

Do you think Demon Slayer has another fight that has a similar level of emotional impact? Or you can head down to the comments to share your favorite fight in the series.

title: 5 Great Shonen Jump Manga Ended in 2026
content:
When it comes to Shonen action and drama, Weekly Shonen Jump always grabs the spotlight, and this has been the case for many decades now. Established in 1968, it eventually became the best-selling manga magazine of all time. A lot of its popularity is thanks to Dragon Ball, One Piece , and many other Shonen classics that kept the magazine running. However, while several of these classics received anime, not all of them got the adaptations they deserve. While the 2000s were a golden era for Shonen fans, many incredible anime suffered from poor pacing and cancellations.

The year is almost over, and Shueisha has already seen major changes in the Weekly Shonen Jump magazine and the official Shonen Jump+ platform. While the platform offers a wide range of series, WSJ has a rather limited lineup. Despite being serialized under the banner of Shonen Jump, a majority of the series don’t often get the attention they deserve and end up being cancelled. Manga series that aren’t performing well take up slots and incur losses to the publisher when the volumes get printed. This results in the series being discontinued abruptly, though unofficially, while some just reach their natural conclusion.

5) Otr of the Flame

Yuki Kawaguchi’s Otr of the Flame made its Shonen Jump debut in May 2025, and after 34 chapters, it came to a close this January. Set in a world where the Ice Kingdom causes harsh, wintry conditions to persist, the story follows a cook who wishes to become a warrior — and gets the opportunity when the enemy arrives on his doorstep.

In terms of plot, the series has a lot of potential, but its pacing and execution never quite reach it. That’s a theme for Shonen Jump ‘s cancelled series of 2026, but the strength of this series’ artwork makes its fate especially tragic. It’s really a shame this one didn’t work out, but leave it to Shonen Jump ‘s first cancelled series of the year to hit the hardest. With a bit more direction, Otr of the Flame could’ve been a gripping ride.

4) Jujutsu Kaisen Modulo

The Jujutsu Kaisen manga reached its controversial ending in September 2024, leaving behind several unanswered questions. Only a year after the finale, Gege Akutami returned with a sequel manga that completely turned the world of Jujutsu Kaisen upside down. While Akutami served as the series’ writer, Yuji Iwasaki provided the gorgeous illustrations that fans can’t stop praising. The story takes place 68 years after the Culling Game, following new characters, including the grandchildren of Yuta Okkotsu, who were introduced in the epilogue.

The most shocking part of the sequel is how it explores sci-fi themes with aliens, also known as Simurians, who came to Japan as refugees. As the story continued, it focused primarily on the struggles between the sorcerers and the Simurians as their differences made it all the more impossible for them to co-exist.

3) Sakamoto Days

Yuto Suzuki’s Sakamoto Days has now officially come to an end with Shonen Jump with the release of Chapter 284, six years after it originally made its debut. The series has been in the midst of its final arc for the past year, so fans have been preparing to say goodbye to the series for quite some time. But with many more fans assuming it would end earlier this Summer, the story was able to take its time and reach a more conclusive finale than many other Shonen Jump titles get .

Sakamoto’s dream of turning his convenience store into a franchise has also worked with a chain of stores across the region, and the final chapter reveals how each of the survivors (both friends and former foes) has since gone on to live new lives that don’t focus on killing. It’s a bright future for everyone as the world finds a new era of peace after everything that’s happened, and it’s clear that Sakamoto has indeed had an impact on everyone he’s come across through his time as a deadly killer.

2) Witch Watch

Witch Watch Chapter 270 officially brings Kenta Shinohara’s long-running manga to an end after a year-long final arc that saw Morihito and the others taking on some very tough foes. The final chapter of the series moves ahead seven years and reveals what happened to everyone after the final battle. The group all decided to stay living together until after graduation, then went their separate ways after a while. Morihito and Nico ended up marrying and having a child together (who is nine months old by the time of the final chapter).

With Witch Watch creator Kenta Shinohara confirming that there will be some additional pages featuring more of the characters after the grand finale, it’s a hope that fans will get some of the closure they had been hoping to see that was absent from the final chapter. With it jumping years into the future, yet still teasing that all of the group would still be hanging out together, fans were hoping to just see more of the wacky adventures that drew them to the series in the first place.

1) Black Clover

The final few chapters of Black Clover wrapped up the long-running story fairly quickly and gave fans a suitable ending for Asta and many of the other characters as they moved into the future following the war against Lucius Zogratis. Though it’s now been confirmed that Tabata will be continuing the manga with a new special chapter coming later this August, so it’s time to try and figure out what kind of epilogue that Tabata is going to offer for the long-running series.

Black Clover is going to continue with an expanded ending after the release of its grand finale, and it’s time to get ready for what could be coming next. Yuki Tabata officially kicked off the final arc of Black Clover ‘s run a few years ago after it left the pages of Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine and moved to a quarterly release schedule where fans got to see a few chapters launched every few months. Wrapping up this final arc earlier this Spring, Black Clover ‘s manga ended after 11 years of serialization.

What are your thoughts on the finale of these Shonen Jump series? Do you hope that any of these have lasted longer? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: New Dragon Ball Super Remake Is Hurting the Anime More Than Helping
content:
Dragon Ball Super : Beerus is a huge disappointment after the Battle of Gods arc, which featured the main battle between Goku and Beerus. The anime returned this month as part of the Fall 2026 lineup, but instead of continuing the story with a sequel, Toei Animation released a remake version of the previous arcs. Since the anime returned after more than eight years, it’s no surprise that the hype was greater than ever, even if the new anime was a remake rather than a sequel. The biggest reason why fans were hyped over the anime’s return is that it aimed to fix the biggest issues with the original anime adaptations, including the animation quality and the pacing.

The remake is following the original story written by Akira Toriyama, the original manga creator, while also focusing on better visuals and fight choreography. A few episodes have already been out, and it’s obvious the new version is drawn from scratch instead of simply polishing the visuals. While the title is Dragon Ball Super: Beerus , the anime will retell the story of the Battle of Gods, Resurrection F, and Universe 6 arcs during its run. However, despite fan expectations, the remake isn’t as good as the studio claimed, and the third episode made it quite clear.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Disappoints With Vegeta’s Character Development

One look at the episode and you can tell easily why it was flamed online by everyone. Not even the biggest fans of the anime could defend the third episode of the remake, and it’s really no surprise considering the rushed pacing and the jarring visuals. During the episode, Beerus arrived on Earth after crushing Goku on King Kai’s planet. However, Vegeta was there to keep things under control. King Kai had already warned him that the God of Destruction would be arriving on the planet, and it’d be best to avoid angering him. In order to save those around him and the planet, Vegeta was even willing to let go of his pride and do all the unnecessary jumping around, even if it made him look like a fool.

He served Beerus and Whis and did everything he could to make sure that none of the other Z Fighters would offend him in any way. Whether it was serving them a plate or dancing, Vegeta utterly humiliated himself in front of everyone. However, while some fans may think it was cringe or irrelevant, these moments highlighted how far he had come since his introduction. Someone as prideful as him was doing everything he could to save the planet, even if it meant bending to Beerus’ will.

As a child, Vegeta had already witnessed the horror Beerus invoked in those around him, which is all the more reason why those moments made sense and added to his character depth. However, most of those moments were original, which is why the anime removed them in the remake. Even so, there’s no denying that some of those added more to the character depth as compared to simply rushing things down and skipping over to the main battle.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Fails to Keep Its Promise of a More Polished Version

It’s not just Vegeta, but the remake made every side character non-existent, which is a huge disappointment. The anime movie, Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods , was released before the Dragon Ball Super manga. While the movie didn’t actually follow the manga, it was already considered canon since the script and everything else was overseen by Akira Toriyama. Later on, the Battle of Gods was included in the manga for only four chapters, but the anime extended the arc with more scenes. The anime series highlighted the side characters even more, especially before Goku jumped into action. Not to mention that it also changed the moment where Beerus slapped Bulma.

Instead of hitting her purposefully, the remake showed that Beerus accidentally hit her with his shoulder , which got Vegeta completely enraged. In the original anime, Vegeta tried his best to avoid a confrontation until he saw his wife being hit by the God of Destruction. Despite his fear and knowing he couldn’t win, he jumped straight into action, landing some of his most powerful attacks on Beerus. The remake was a great idea, but the execution was poorly handled. Some of the scenes remain the same while others changed completely. Not to mention that the visuals and filters aren’t as good as the anime promised, which is yet another major disappointment.

The anime had quite a lot of time to fix the issues with the previous versions, but it still didn’t change some of the drawings that needed corrections. While the remake was supposed to be a better version of the anime, at this point it’s pretty evident what fans prefer. Since the remake turned out to be a huge disappointment in only the first few weeks, there’s no denying that the next episodes will feature the same jarring color scheme and rushed pacing that completely took the heart and soul of the story away.

Do you think Dragon Ball Super: Beerus can turn things around later since the first arc has already raised concerns about how it will handle the biggest battles? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Live-Action This World is Worth Fighting For Series Casts Ikoi Hayase
content:
The official website for the live-action series of Hatsumi Kodama 's This World is Worth Fighting For ( Konoyo wa Tatakau Kachi ga Aru ) manga announced on Friday that Ikoi Hayase (live-action Journal with Witch /Worlds Apart, Cursed Meme, Ano Ko wa Daare?) is joining the series' cast. Hayase plays Yūka Kitayama, a teenager who took over running her family's liquor store when her father was unable to bounce back from his wife's death in a hit-and-run accident.

Seven Seas licensed the manga, and it describes the story:

Ito Kiri has had enough. She's 25, is in her third year at a company she hates where she's also getting sexually harassed, and dating a shitty guy. She exists solely on energy drinks and one thought: “I want to be useful to others.” But she's beginning to reach her limit and feeling hopeless about her future. That is, until she receives a mysterious letter one day. No return address, no name, just a message she needed: Permission to live freely and on her terms. From that moment, something changes in her and she decides she's doing whatever it takes to live a life worth living. And she's not holding back or pulling any punches.

Hiyori Sakurada stars in the live-action series as Ito Kiri.

Kaede Kamiya is directing the live-action series. Yasuko Kuramitsu is writing the scripts.

The live-action series will premiere on Fuji TV and affiliated channels in January 2027.

Kodama debuted the manga in Shogakukan 's Big Comic Spirits magazine in April 2023, and ended it in October 2025. The fifth and final compiled book volume shipped in Japan on January 30.

title: No Longer Heroine's Momoko Kōda Launches New Manga on December 21
content:
Manga creator Momoko Kōda announced on November 20 that they will launch a new manga titled Kono Oto, Myaku Ari Desu ka? (Is This Sound a Pulse of Interest?) on Shueisha 's Manga Mee web platform on December 21. The manga teases an unlikely romance between a novel-writing (but romantically inexperienced) girl who dreams of her one true love, and a playboy doctor.

Kōda launched the Atashino! (Mine!) manga in Shueisha 's Bessatsu Margaret magazine in September 2017. The manga ended with tis fourth volume in January 2019. The manga inspired a live-action film in 2024.

Kōda's 10-volume No Longer Heroine ( Heroine Shikkaku ) manga ran in Bessatsu Margaret from 2010 to 2013, and inspired a live-action film in September 2015. Yen Press released the manga in English.

Kōda launched the My Special One ( Kimi ga Tokubetsu ) manga in Bessatsu Margaret in March 2019. The manga went on hiatus in October 2022 due to Kōda's poor health, but resumed serialization in June 2024. The series then ended in January 2025. Viz Media publishes the manga in English. The manga was also adapted into a live-action film and live-action television series in June and September last year, respectively.

title: Isekai Affair Writer Masakazu Ooi Launches New Manga
content:
Shogakukan 's online magazine Weekly CoroCoro Comic launched Masakazu Ooi 's new manga Ma Mama Musō~Maō no Mama ni Amae Makuttara Saikyō ni! Saijaku Skill "Amaenbō" de Musōshite Akugyaku Yūsha ni Fukushūshimasu (Ma Mama Musō: Becoming the Strongest by Being Utterly Pampered by the Demon Lord's Mama! Using the Weakest Skill "Spoiled Child" to Become Unrivaled and Take Revenge on the Wicked Hero) on Friday.

The manga centers on Solo, a dull boy who grew up without knowing his mother. He joins his childhood friend, the archetypal hero, on a quest to defeat the Demon Lord, but the hero betrays Solo upon their triumphant return to the kingdom, leaving him in despair. A chance encounter with the Demon Lord's mother activates Solo's "Spoiled Child" skill, and he gains overwhelming power as the Demon Lord's mother thoroughly pampers him. Solo then sets to exact revenge on the hero.

Ooi and artist Inomaru launched the ISEKAI AFFAIR: 10 Years After Defeating the Demon King, the Hero Cheats on His Wife With a Warrior Woman Who Lost Her Husband manga on Shogakukan 's Sunday Webry website in December 2020. The manga's third and final compiled book volume shipped in December 2021. Seven Seas licensed the manga and released the third volume in September 2025.

The duo then launched the Isekai Furin II - Michibikareshi Hitozuma-tachi to Bukiyō Tensei Yūsha ( ISEKAI AFFAIR II: Guided Wives and Clumsy Otherworld Heroes) spinoff manga in November 2021 on Shogakukan 's Sunday Webry website. The manga ended in its ninth and final volume, which published in January 2025.

The duo launched the ongoing Ura Dungeon Oku-san (The Secret Dungeon Wife) manga in Shogakukan 's Monthly Sunday GX magazine in April 2025. Ooi is credited for the original story, and Inomaru is drawing the manga. Shogakukan published the manga's fifth volume on November 18.
